claims.text: The driver's continuous presence inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius never reached the 300 second minimum that POL-NS-01(c) requires. The trace's own accumulation splits his in-geofence time into two runs - 220 s from 12:30:00 to 12:33:40, then 112 s from 12:36:28 to 12:38:20 - and reports longest_run_sec of 220 s with a shortfall_sec of 80 s against the 300 s STANDARD minimum. I disclose that EV-GPS-00211 is impaired (issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE, weight 0.39); the outage is the very reason the run was broken, and the discount does not restore the missing 80 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the $4.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full.

The 500 s longest_qualifying_run figure cannot be used to satisfy the dwell: it is a span drawn across the outage, not a demonstrated presence through it. Its fix_count of 35 is exactly the sum of the two split runs' 23 and 12 fixes, so not one fix inside 12:33:40-12:36:28 places the driver in the geofence. Reading the presence as a single 500 s run, or as an accumulated 332 s, is reachable only by adding the two intervals together - which is what POL-NS-06(i) permits solely where a present and populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road. EV-ADVIS-00211-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, so limb (i) is unavailable, the separate intervals may not be summed and the gap may not be bridged. I cite that artifact only for its absence, as POL-GEN-02 permits.

POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and limb (c) is not met, so the fee is not chargeable at all and POL-NS-07 cannot be engaged to pay the driver. Limbs (a) and (b) do hold - the trip record carries an arrived event at 12:29:55 and the trace puts the driver 18.1 to 29.3 m from the pin at 6.1 to 11.9 m accuracy (EV-GPS-00211, impaired, GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE, weight 0.39) - but limb (c) fails on the 220 s run, and limb (d) fails with it, because the driver terminated the trip at 12:38:20 on RIDER_NO_SHOW before any 300 s continuous dwell had elapsed. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 satisfied in full; it is not, so no driver compensation is payable and the fee cannot stand.

The admissibility pre-pass on EV-GPS-00211 records a 168 s outage from 12:33:40 to 12:36:28 falling inside the waiting window, and states in terms that whether the driver stayed put across those 168 seconds is not established by this trace. A sampling gap over 120 s inside the waiting window is a trace defect under POL-NS-08(b), so any dwell finding that depends on reading the outage as presence is down-weighted under POL-GEN-02 as well as at schema level. The rider's shortfall point does not depend on the gap at all: it stands on the two intervals that were actually measured.

The driver's 12:35:10 message, 'boss still here waiting ah, cannot see you', shows he was still working the pickup during the outage, but it is his own unsworn assertion and carries no coordinates. POL-NS-01(c) requires the gps_trace to hold the driver inside the geofence for the dwell, and the chat log records nothing about position; a chat message cannot bridge a 168 second trace gap that the trace itself cannot bridge, and it is in any event a statement about his own conduct rather than a fix. The chat log is otherwise clean - five entries, matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 5, weight 1.0 - so the driver has no chat-side defect to complain of either.

The rider was at the pickup and not absent: her device logged 36 of 55 fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius (mean 81.8 m, closest 24.6 m), and she messaged 'coming down now, 2 min' at 12:31:02, read by the driver at 12:31:15. I disclose that those positions come from EV-GPS-00211, impaired at weight 0.39. Her conduct is in any event not the test: POL-NS-06 refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. I note candidly that POL-NS-04 is not available to her, because the driver did reply at 12:31:20, inside the 120 second window that limb (b) of that clause requires.

If the judge prefers the driver's reading and treats the 168 s outage as presence, the deciding fact - whether the driver held the geofence across that interval - is then carried by no usable evidence at all: the only artifact bearing on it is EV-GPS-00211, impaired under POL-NS-08(b) at weight 0.39, which caps confidence below the 0.70 platform floor under POL-GEN-02(2), requires under POL-NS-08 that the ruling not exceed PARTIAL_REFUND, and escalates under POL-NS-09 with the disputed $4.00 held rather than collected or refunded while review is pending. On no reading of this record does the rider end up funding this charge.

The refund figure is exact and there is no fare-integrity complication: the fare breakdown charges a $4.00 cancellation fee, which is both the STANDARD zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee, so the two prescribe the same amount and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation-fee line only, so the sum to be returned to this rider is exactly $4.00.

claims.text: POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are satisfied on the trip record. It carries a driver 'arrived' event at 12:29:55, no boarding event and no trip start, and it shows the trip terminated BY THE DRIVER at 12:38:20 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. The termination came 8 minutes 25 seconds after the arrival event, so it was at or after the moment any required dwell elapsed.

POL-NS-01 limb (b) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are satisfied. The driver's trace holds 23 consecutive fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, sitting 18.1 m to 29.3 m from the pickup pin at 6.1 m to 11.9 m reported accuracy, well inside the 25 m accuracy filter, running from 12:30:00. The first in-geofence fix is five seconds from the 12:29:55 arrival marker and the derived dwell_start_offset_sec is -5.0 s; there is no clock-skew finding here and POL-NS-08(a) would require more than 90 seconds before that match could be called unsafe.

POL-NS-01 limb (c) is met on the trace's own arrival computation: the driver's qualifying in-geofence presence runs from the first qualifying fix at 12:30:00 to cancellation at 12:38:20, 500 seconds, against the 300 second minimum for STANDARD. I disclose that EV-GPS-00211 is IMPAIRED - weight 0.39, issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE - because a 168 second device outage from 12:33:40 to 12:36:28 falls inside that span. The impairment does not carry the rider's point: an outage is the ABSENCE of fixes, not a fix showing the driver outside the radius. The last fix before the gap and the first after place him in the same place 18.1 m to 29.3 m from the pin, and the one unimpaired artifact covering the outage, chat message MSG-00211-004 sent at 12:35:10, shows him still working the pickup. A trace that cannot show him leaving cannot establish that he left, and so cannot establish a shortfall.

The 'arrived' marker at 12:29:55 is not a false arrival under POL-NS-05, so the waiting clock runs from the marker as recorded and needs no recomputation. At the marker the driver's device reported 18.1 m from the pin - far inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, nowhere near the 300 m distance trigger - and the trace reports a 0.0 km/h speed alongside his stationary kerbside hold, so the 15 km/h motion trigger is not met either. Limb (iii) of POL-NS-05 applies: the marker is genuine, and it does not defeat the fee.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. That clause requires that the driver posted no reply within 120 seconds of the rider's coordinating message AND placed no in-app call. The rider wrote 'coming down now, 2 min' at 12:31:02 and the driver replied 'ok waiting outside 79' at 12:31:20 - 18 seconds later, well inside the window - and posted again at 12:35:10. Limb (b) fails on its face, so POL-NS-04 does not apply regardless of the content of the reply, and the driver's answer also disposes of any in_app_calls point since the record shows an empty call list.

The rider's own words fix the fault on her side of the transaction. She said 'coming down now, 2 min' at 12:31:02, the system had announced arrival at 12:29:56, and she said nothing further until her post-cancellation 'eh why cancel, i was at the door already' at 12:38:45 - more than seven minutes after promising two. Against that silence the driver's 12:35:10 'boss still here waiting ah, cannot see you' is the record of a driver who was still on the kerb trying to complete the pickup when the rider had not appeared.

POL-NS-01 being satisfied, compensation follows under POL-NS-07 and the anti-farming check does not withhold it. That check needs BOTH limbs: no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND a termination rate above 0.08. The driver's no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below 4, and 2 terminations across 146 completed trips is 1.4 per cent, far below 8 per cent, so neither limb is met and there is no pattern to withhold against. A verified rider no-show therefore pays the driver 80 per cent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee itemised in the fare breakdown - SGD 3.20 - with the residual 20 per cent retained as the platform service fee.

Even on the reading most favourable to the rider, this case cannot produce a rider refund. The dwell finding is carried by a single artifact, EV-GPS-00211, and that artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b) itself, not merely at schema level: a 168 second sampling gap inside the waiting window exceeds the 120 second limb, which is the same defect the pre-pass tagged at weight 0.39. Where the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under limbs (a) to (d), the ruling may not exceed PARTIAL_REFUND and the case escalates under POL-NS-09; escalation holds the disputed SGD 4.00 rather than collecting or refunding it, so the charge is not reversed while the human reviewer settles whether the driver held the kerb across the outage.

This case goes to a human reviewer. No money moves in the meantime: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded, and no compensation is paid, until the reviewer settles the single question set out at the end.

What the case turns on. The driver may keep the fee only if POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and the disputed limb is (c): he must have held position inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous 300 seconds. That fact can only come from the GPS trace EV-GPS-00211, and that trace is impaired. A 168-second sampling gap runs from 12:33:40 to 12:36:28, inside the waiting window, and the artifact carries weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE. This is a policy-level defect and not merely a schema tag: POL-NS-08(b) makes a gap longer than 120 seconds inside the waiting window an impairment.

The gap straddles the exact moment the minimum would elapse. The trace measures continuous in-geofence presence for 220 seconds, from 12:30:00 to 12:33:40. The 300-second mark falls at 12:35:00, which is 80 seconds inside the unobserved stretch. Whether the driver stayed on the kerb across those 80 seconds is precisely what the trace cannot show. Limb (c) is therefore undecided over that stretch — neither satisfied nor failed — and an undecided limb supports neither a charge that needs it to hold nor a refund that needs it to fail.

Why the separate runs may not be added. POL-NS-06(i) permits two in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated traffic advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road. EV-ADVIS-00211-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, so summation is unavailable and the two runs (220 s and 112 s) may not be added into 332 seconds.

Your point that the arrival marker is genuine is accepted: at 12:29:55 the trace puts you 18.1 m from the pin at 0 km/h, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged and the waiting clock needs no recomputation, and there is no clock-skew defect (the first qualifying fix is 5 seconds from the marker, far inside the 90-second limb). Your POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) points are accepted — an arrived event, no boarding, and a driver cancellation at 12:38:20 on RIDER_NO_SHOW. Your POL-NS-04 point is accepted: the rider's 12:31:02 message was answered at 12:31:20, so that clause does not apply. But your limb (c) point rests on the trace's 500-second 'longest_qualifying_run', and that figure is a span drawn across the outage, not a certified presence through it — it is the very bridging POL-NS-06(i) forbids without the missing advisory. Your POL-NS-07 compensation claim (SGD 3.20) therefore cannot be paid: POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full while limb (c) is undecided, and escalation holds all money. The anti-farming check would not have withheld compensation (2 no-show terminations in 146 trips), but that creates no entitlement here.

Your POL-NS-06 arithmetic is right on its own terms — the longest measured continuous run is 220 seconds, an 80-second shortfall — but it reads the unobserved 80 seconds as absence, and an outage is the absence of fixes, not a fix showing the driver outside the radius. Because limb (c) is undecided rather than failed, it cannot support a refund. Your point that the 12:35:10 message carries no coordinates is well taken: it shows the driver was still working the pickup but not where he was, and POL-NS-01(c) reads the gps_trace, so an account cannot decide the limb. It is a contemporaneous record from inside the unobserved stretch, so it counts as a bridging record; but it records activity, not position, so it neither decides the limb nor carries the deciding fact, and the trace remains the only artifact that does. Your fare point is accepted: the fare breakdown's SGD 4.00 equals both the STANDARD zone fee and the RYDE_X tier fee, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and the refund figure, were one due, would be exact.

Confidence. The deciding fact — the driver's continuous in-geofence position — is carried only by the impaired trace. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap is that artifact's own weight, 0.39, which is below the platform-wide floor of 0.70.

Two triggers under POL-NS-09 are met: Judge confidence is below the 0.70 floor (limb (a)), and the sole evidence for the deciding fact is an artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(b) (limb (e)). Escalation is terminal and replaces a monetary ruling, and no clause displaced here directs a separate referral.

The open question for the reviewer: whether the driver held position within the 50 m arrival radius continuously from 12:30:00 to at least 12:35:00 — that is, across the 12:33:40 to 12:36:28 gap — and whether any traffic advisory covering the pickup road was in force in that window, which would allow the two separate in-geofence intervals to be summed.

Its fix_count of 35 is exactly the sum of the two split runs' 23 and 12 fixes, so not one fix inside 12:33:40-12:36:28 places the driver in the geofence. Reading the presence as a single 500 s run, or as an accumulated 332 s, is reachable only by adding the two intervals together - which is what POL-NS-06(i) permits solely where a present and populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road. EV-ADVIS-00211-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, so limb (i) is unavailable, the separate intervals may not be summed and the gap may not be bridged. I cite that artifact only for its absence, as POL-GEN-02 permits.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and limb (c) is not met, so the fee is not chargeable at all and POL-NS-07 cannot be engaged to pay the driver. Limbs (a) and (b) do hold - the trip record carries an arrived event at 12:29:55 and the trace puts the driver 18.1 to 29.3 m from the pin at 6.1 to 11.9 m accuracy (EV-GPS-00211, impaired, GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE, weight 0.39) - but limb (c) fails on the 220 s run, and limb (d) fails with it, because the driver terminated the trip at 12:38:20 on RIDER_NO_SHOW before any 300 s continuous dwell had elapsed. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 satisfied in full; it is not, so no driver compensation is payable and the fee cannot stand.

The admissibility pre-pass on EV-GPS-00211 records a 168 s outage from 12:33:40 to 12:36:28 falling inside the waiting window, and states in terms that whether the driver stayed put across those 168 seconds is not established by this trace. A sampling gap over 120 s inside the waiting window is a trace defect under POL-NS-08(b), so any dwell finding that depends on reading the outage as presence is down-weighted under POL-GEN-02 as well as at schema level. The rider's shortfall point does not depend on the gap at all: it stands on the two intervals that were actually measured.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-00211 at weight_multiplier 0.39 but does not name its issue code(s): GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE

ledger.claim: The driver's 12:35:10 message, 'boss still here waiting ah, cannot see you', shows he was still working the pickup during the outage, but it is his own unsworn assertion and carries no coordinates. POL-NS-01(c) requires the gps_trace to hold the driver inside the geofence for the dwell, and the chat log records nothing about position; a chat message cannot bridge a 168 second trace gap that the trace itself cannot bridge, and it is in any event a statement about his own conduct rather than a fix. The chat log is otherwise clean - five entries, matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 5, weight 1.0 - so the driver has no chat-side defect to complain of either.

The rider was at the pickup and not absent: her device logged 36 of 55 fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius (mean 81.8 m, closest 24.6 m), and she messaged 'coming down now, 2 min' at 12:31:02, read by the driver at 12:31:15. I disclose that those positions come from EV-GPS-00211, impaired at weight 0.39. Her conduct is in any event not the test: POL-NS-06 refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. I note candidly that POL-NS-04 is not available to her, because the driver did reply at 12:31:20, inside the 120 second window that limb (b) of that clause requires.

ledger.claim: If the judge prefers the driver's reading and treats the 168 s outage as presence, the deciding fact - whether the driver held the geofence across that interval - is then carried by no usable evidence at all: the only artifact bearing on it is EV-GPS-00211, impaired under POL-NS-08(b) at weight 0.39, which caps confidence below the 0.70 platform floor under POL-GEN-02(2), requires under POL-NS-08 that the ruling not exceed PARTIAL_REFUND, and escalates under POL-NS-09 with the disputed $4.00 held rather than collected or refunded while review is pending. On no reading of this record does the rider end up funding this charge.

ledger.claim: The refund figure is exact and there is no fare-integrity complication: the fare breakdown charges a $4.00 cancellation fee, which is both the STANDARD zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee, so the two prescribe the same amount and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation-fee line only, so the sum to be returned to this rider is exactly $4.00.

POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are satisfied on the trip record. It carries a driver 'arrived' event at 12:29:55, no boarding event and no trip start, and it shows the trip terminated BY THE DRIVER at 12:38:20 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. The termination came 8 minutes 25 seconds after the arrival event, so it was at or after the moment any required dwell elapsed.

POL-NS-01 limb (b) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are satisfied. The driver's trace holds 23 consecutive fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, sitting 18.1 m to 29.3 m from the pickup pin at 6.1 m to 11.9 m reported accuracy, well inside the 25 m accuracy filter, running from 12:30:00. The first in-geofence fix is five seconds from the 12:29:55 arrival marker and the derived dwell_start_offset_sec is -5.0 s; there is no clock-skew finding here and POL-NS-08(a) would require more than 90 seconds before that match could be called unsafe.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 limb (c) is met on the trace's own arrival computation: the driver's qualifying in-geofence presence runs from the first qualifying fix at 12:30:00 to cancellation at 12:38:20, 500 seconds, against the 300 second minimum for STANDARD. I disclose that EV-GPS-00211 is IMPAIRED - weight 0.39, issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE - because a 168 second device outage from 12:33:40 to 12:36:28 falls inside that span. The impairment does not carry the rider's point: an outage is the ABSENCE of fixes, not a fix showing the driver outside the radius. The last fix before the gap and the first after place him in the same place 18.1 m to 29.3 m from the pin, and the one unimpaired artifact covering the outage, chat message MSG-00211-004 sent at 12:35:10, shows him still working the pickup. A trace that cannot show him leaving cannot establish that he left, and so cannot establish a shortfall.

The 'arrived' marker at 12:29:55 is not a false arrival under POL-NS-05, so the waiting clock runs from the marker as recorded and needs no recomputation. At the marker the driver's device reported 18.1 m from the pin - far inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, nowhere near the 300 m distance trigger - and the trace reports a 0.0 km/h speed alongside his stationary kerbside hold, so the 15 km/h motion trigger is not met either. Limb (iii) of POL-NS-05 applies: the marker is genuine, and it does not defeat the fee.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. That clause requires that the driver posted no reply within 120 seconds of the rider's coordinating message AND placed no in-app call. The rider wrote 'coming down now, 2 min' at 12:31:02 and the driver replied 'ok waiting outside 79' at 12:31:20 - 18 seconds later, well inside the window - and posted again at 12:35:10. Limb (b) fails on its face, so POL-NS-04 does not apply regardless of the content of the reply, and the driver's answer also disposes of any in_app_calls point since the record shows an empty call list.

The rider's own words fix the fault on her side of the transaction. She said 'coming down now, 2 min' at 12:31:02, the system had announced arrival at 12:29:56, and she said nothing further until her post-cancellation 'eh why cancel, i was at the door already' at 12:38:45 - more than seven minutes after promising two. Against that silence the driver's 12:35:10 'boss still here waiting ah, cannot see you' is the record of a driver who was still on the kerb trying to complete the pickup when the rider had not appeared.

POL-NS-01 being satisfied, compensation follows under POL-NS-07 and the anti-farming check does not withhold it. That check needs BOTH limbs: no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND a termination rate above 0.08. The driver's no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below 4, and 2 terminations across 146 completed trips is 1.4 per cent, far below 8 per cent, so neither limb is met and there is no pattern to withhold against. A verified rider no-show therefore pays the driver 80 per cent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee itemised in the fare breakdown - SGD 3.20 - with the residual 20 per cent retained as the platform service fee.

Even on the reading most favourable to the rider, this case cannot produce a rider refund. The dwell finding is carried by a single artifact, EV-GPS-00211, and that artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b) itself, not merely at schema level: a 168 second sampling gap inside the waiting window exceeds the 120 second limb, which is the same defect the pre-pass tagged at weight 0.39. Where the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under limbs (a) to (d), the ruling may not exceed PARTIAL_REFUND and the case escalates under POL-NS-09; escalation holds the disputed SGD 4.00 rather than collecting or refunding it, so the charge is not reversed while the human reviewer settles whether the driver held the kerb across the outage.
